newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end strong on telcom, foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end strong on telcom, foreign buying.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended firm in heavy trade boosted by a surge in telecommunications stocks and increased foreign buys, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares ended up 2.12 percent at 91,491 points. Market turnover was a high 770.1 million reais ($733.8 million), traders said.

Analysts said speculation that a new tariff rebalancing could take place any time soon prompted players to buy telecom stocks, particularly bellwether Telebras preferred which climbed 2.59 percent to 106.80 reais.
Telebras' common stock also surged 3.39 percent to 103.70 reais.
The latest rate adjustment occurred in November 1995 and was one of the main factors behind Telebras' 1996 earnings, which are likely to come out some time this week.

Analysts also said the local bolsa still reflected optimism over the future of the government's plans to privatize the Band B cellular services after a judge on Monday rejected an injunction which would suspend the cellular bidding process.
"The market is still upbeat on the judge's decision," said Jose Domingo Gonzalez y Bouzon, director of newly formed Maturity asset management firm.

Eased concerns that a congressional investigation into a fraud sheme involving municipal and state bonds could lead to a broad inquiry into the financial sector also helped bolstering the market, he said.
Last week the Central Bank liquidated more than 10 small financial institutions for their role in the fraud that may have led to money laundering.
Among other top blue-chips, state oil firm Petrobras
State mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce jumped 3.71 percent to 28.50 reais after news that a draft of the tender documents for the firm's upcoming selloff could be out Friday.
Analysts said local shares could continue climbing Wednesday despite possible selling pressure from investors interested in taking profits after two days of strong rises.
"I think the market may absorb profit-taking movements during the session," said one trader.
